features.name: Serial routing
features.description: Routing type where operations run one after another in sequence. Each operation includes details such as location and operational times.

features.name: Parallel routing
features.description: Routing type where multiple independent operations can run at the same time to reduce total lead time. After an initial operation, workload is split and both run simultaneously.

features.name: Operational times
features.description: Time components in routing operations including setup time, run time, wait time, and move time. These directly influence scheduling and cost calculations.

features.name: Routing link code
features.description: Field that connects a component to a specific operation, enabling material consumption when that operation runs for just-in-time material control.

features.name: Send ahead quantity
features.description: Field that lets the next operation start before the current one finishes, overlapping steps to reduce total lead time.

features.name: Standard tasks in routing operations
features.description: Standard tasks can be attached to operations to simplify recurring activities and maintain consistency in documentation.

features.name: Routing versions
features.description: Feature allowing creation of new routing versions when production process changes, preserving the original version.

features.name: Production order automatic routing population
features.description: When creating a production order, Business Central automatically populates item lines with the required BOM and routing, and computes production times including starting and ending dates.

features.name: Production order modification
features.description: Ability to modify production orders to use different routings for different quantities, such as using parallel routing for some units and serial routing for others.

features.name: Lead time calculation and optimization
features.description: Production times are computed from routing times and available capacities. More resources reduce lead times, and parallel routing allows starting production at a later date by utilizing simultaneous operations.

quotes.text: Just like the BOM defines what you need, the routing describes the sequence of operations required to build the product.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the fundamental role of routing in manufacturing - it defines the how, complementing the BOM which defines the what.

quotes.text: Routings support both serial operations, where steps run one after another, and parallel operations, when two independent activities can run at the same time.
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the two core routing types and their fundamental difference, showing Business Central accommodates different production strategies.

quotes.text: Operational times include setup time, run time, wait time, and move time between operations.
quotes.why_it_matters: Identifies the specific time components that directly influence scheduling and cost calculations in manufacturing.

quotes.text: Routing link code connects a component to a specific operation, so the material is consumed when that operation runs, giving you just-in-time material control.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains a key mechanism for achieving just-in-time material consumption in production, affecting material planning.

quotes.text: Business Central supports routing versions, allowing you to create a new version when your process changes without losing the original.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows how Business Central manages process evolution while maintaining historical data - a design choice that supports process improvement.

quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the practical lead time benefit of parallel routing - starting later but finishing on time through concurrent operations.
